scope: B2wPiper, OFFICIAL ATEC-TaskB-B2wPiper env, single env, seed 42, cameras ENABLED and recorded from a third-person overview camera. ORACLE probe: the base is parked from the object's true pose, so this measures and shows the delivery mechanics, not perception or a policy.
claim: The official objects_in_circle reward fires while the run is on camera, in a third-person view that shows the whole robot and the bin. This is the same oracle delivery as task_b/results/oracle_delivery.json; it is not a policy result and not a Task B pass.

layout.main_view: third-person overview camera, mounted on base_link at (-2.00, -2.00, 1.25) m and aimed at the body-frame point (0.15, 0.00, 0.20) m, world-up level, 24 mm focal length
layout.insets: head RGB and wrist RGB, 448x336 each, bottom-left, labelled
layout.title_bar: mode, policy seconds, raw score, layout
layout.why_changed: the first delivery recording used only the two onboard 640x480 cameras, which are low resolution and pointed at the work rather than at the robot. This adds the same kind of chase camera the Task A videos use.
layout.framing_check: task_b/audit_overview_video.py, reproducible on CPU. Against the in-repo body-frame robot envelope the chosen mount keeps the nearest frame edge 77.2 px away (30 px floor) and spans 42.1 percent of the frame width; the earlier Task-A-style (-2.30,-2.30,1.70) mount put part of that envelope 43.5 px outside the frame and spanned 35.6 percent. Against the points the run actually recorded -- the gripper and the held object -- the earlier mount had 209.6 px of margin and this one 316.0 px, so nothing was clipped in either recording: the gain is headroom and apparent size, not the rescue of a clipped frame.

reproduces_the_earlier_runs_exactly.note: identical step count, identical score to six significant figures and the same two scoring steps across the camera-free run, the onboard-camera run and this third-person run

source_video.kept_where: too large for the repository, published as the Release asset task_b_first_delivery_20260915_original.mp4

poster.shows: the arm holding the mustard bottle over the bin, three tenths of a second before the score flips

transformation: full 1x recording, unchanged frame count and timing, no padding needed (the render is already 1920x1080); lossy H.264 re-encode only; no generated frames or edited robot motion
ffmpeg_version: ffmpeg version 4.4.2-0ubuntu0.22.04.1 Copyright (c) 2000-2021 the FFmpeg developers

what_to_watch.timeline_source: the probe's own phase record in trace.jsonl, in policy seconds; the recording is 10 fps against a 50 Hz policy, so a media second spans exactly 50 policy steps and the two clocks track each other; the file is 47.300 s against 47.38 s of policy time because the last frame interval is partial
what_to_watch.0.0_s: REACH -- the two-stage reach begins from the settled stance
what_to_watch.2.7_s: CLOSE -- the jaws close on the bottle
what_to_watch.6.2_s: LIFT -- the bottle leaves the ground
what_to_watch.10.2_s: CARRY -- the drive to the bin, bottle held, 30 s long; the container and its shadow fill the right of the frame as the robot arrives
what_to_watch.40.7_s: PLACE_RAISE -- the bottle comes up over the bin's 0.50 m lip
what_to_watch.43.2_s: PLACE_DRIVE -- the inward move past the wall
what_to_watch.43.9_s: objects_in_circle fires (step 2195). The on-frame raw score flips 1 -> 2.
what_to_watch.46.6_s: RELEASE -- the jaws open and the object drops
what_to_watch.watch_out: The raw score reads 1 from 0.7 s onward. That is the official grasped_objects proximity term firing at spawn -- the gripper body starts within its 0.20 m threshold of an object -- and it is NOT a grasp. The grasp itself is the LIFT at 6.2 s; the second point, at 43.9 s, is the delivery.

caveat: The overlay and the score come from the evaluator. The overview camera is a diagnostic render product added for the recording: it is absent from the official scene, no policy reads it, and it is declared in the run's result.json and source manifest. The speckled ground is the official terrain material, not render noise or compression.
